archetypes.name: shell-retry-semantics
archetypes.rationale: The plan's sync+retry probe and hoisted Bash arithmetic introduce subtle correctness risks that the generic correctness archetype may miss without shell-specific depth.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the proposed step5_probe_prior_round_env retry logic is semantically correct: check whether invoking sync followed by a second [[ -f ]] stat actually defeats the macOS VFS cache described in Hypothesis A, or whether the same cached inode result is returned. Confirm the Bash 3.2 arithmetic in the hoisted cap math handles unset or empty entry_prior_deg without causing (( )) arithmetic errors that silently evaluate to 0. Inspect whether count_prior_degraded_rounds reading a partially-written review-and-fix.env file (written by a concurrent MAV-apply) can return a value that makes entry_effective_cap inconsistent with the within-loop computation later in the same invocation. Check that the helper exit codes (0=found, 1=not-found) are propagated correctly through the caller without being masked by set -e, a subshell boundary, or a trailing || true guard elsewhere in run_implement_loop. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: envelope-consumer-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan flips STALL_TRACKING from true to false for starting-round-invalid and claims no orchestrator code change is needed; that claim must be verified against all downstream consumers before it can be accepted.
archetypes.prompt_body: Enumerate every code path that reads STALL_TRACKING= from a step5_emit_final_envelope output or from the envelope file written to disk, and verify each one correctly handles starting-round-invalid now carrying STALL_TRACKING=false rather than true. Check whether the orchestrator tracking-issue rename step described in skills/implement/SKILL.md or any script guarded on STALL_TRACKING=true will correctly skip the [STALLED] rename when STALL_TRACKING=false is emitted for starting-round-invalid. Confirm the plan's assertion that no orchestrator code change is needed is accurate — specifically that the orchestrator already branches on the parsed STALL_TRACKING value rather than hard-coding per-stall-reason behavior for this stall reason. Identify any location in skills/, scripts/, or docs/ that documents or references starting-round-invalid as a STALL_TRACKING=true case and would become a stale contract after this change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-scaffold-validity
archetypes.rationale: The four proposed test cases make specific isolation and assertion claims about stub wiring and envelope format that require verification against the actual test harness and function internals.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the four proposed test cases in test-review-and-fix.sh correctly isolate run_implement_loop: confirm that stubbing _implement_round_body as a shell function is sufficient to prevent real round execution and that the function is actually invoked via the stub name rather than a differently-named internal callsite within the loop body. Check whether count_prior_degraded_rounds called from the hoisted cap math at function entry requires a live IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR file structure that the test cases must pre-populate in a way consistent with the entry_prior_deg and entry_effective_cap values they assert in their pass/fail criteria. Confirm whether the Hypothesis A simulation (case 3) is achievable with a deterministic shell approach, or whether the plan's COVERAGE_NOTE skip leaves a real regression path untested. Assess whether grep -F 'STALL_TRACKING=false' and grep -F 'STALL_REASON=starting-round-invalid' assertions are robust — specifically whether both tokens are guaranteed to appear on the same output line in the envelope format, or whether a multi-line envelope could cause the co-occurrence assertion to produce a false pass. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
